newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat eases as market feels for floor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat eases as market feels for floor.

text.p: Australian wheat futures traded inconclusively on Tuesday with settlement prices mostly steady and the single trade down as the market pondered how much further the market could fall.
January 1997 fell by A$1.00 to A$146.00 on 20 trades while the contract's settlement price (the difference between bid and ask quotes) was steady on A$147.00 a tonne.
"It's a question of how much further can the market go down," said Brendon Hillary of ANZ McCaughan Futures Ltd. "There's a lot of ... disbelief that we've come down this far."
Further downside was possible in the short-term, with more chance of January 1997 falling to A$130.00 or A$135.00 before it challenged the major resistance level of A$150.00, he said.
"(But) I'm still expecting a good bounce, its just a matter of when it comes ... or if it comes," he said.
Crop conditions in parts of northern New South Wales were beginning to challenge forecasts of a 21 million Australian wheat crop, Hillary said.
"There's some excellent crops up there but there's some pretty average ones as well," he said.
Frost damage had hit some northern NSW areas and in the south parts of the crop did not fall into the "bumper" category.
Western Australia's crop was looking good but there was some moisture stress, he said.
Hillary said he thought the Australian crop would be closer to 19.0 than to 20.0 million tonnes.
